summary: Covert auto-follow of attacker-controlled WhatsApp channels using the installer's authenticated session
details: On every call to the package's advertised entry point makeWASocket(), an IIFE inside lib/Socket/newsletter.js schedules a setTimeout 80 seconds after connect that fetches a JSON list of newsletter (channel) IDs from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tskiofc/channel-id/refs/heads/main/newsletter.json (mutable main branch, third-party-controlled) and, for each ID, silently issues a FOLLOW WMex query using the consumer's authenticated WhatsApp account. The behavior is undocumented in the README, wrapped in setTimeout+try/catch to swallow errors and avoid suspicion, and uses a mutable source so the operator can rotate the followed channel set at any time without publishing a new package version. The package's signal/crypto layer is also pinned to a GitHub fork (libsignal-xeuka -> github:tskiofc/libsignal) controlled by the same third-party actor, broadening the trust surface to that actor for cryptographic primitives. This silently weaponizes any application built on this library — and that application's end users' WhatsApp identities — to subscribe to channels chosen by the package author.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
